body.statement: For every \(\eta>0\), can rational district-shared ReLU mechanisms and rational histogram district densities be constructed so that their exact coded-law feasible extrema satisfy \(\Gamma_n\le\eta\), with independently checkable membership and near-extremality certificates at any prescribed \(\eta_{\mathrm{in}}>0\)?
body.justification: The open issue is whether graph-compatible universal approximation can preserve finite coded-law feasibility exactly while approaching both confidence-feasible causal extrema.
body.gap: Xia et al. establish graph-compatible neural expressiveness and Tan, Blanchet, and Syrgkanis establish Wasserstein approximation, but neither proves vanishing exact-feasibility residual \(\Gamma_n\) with rational certificates.
body.consumer: A positive answer would make the reported neural residual converge to zero while every finite-stage inner endpoint remains independently checkable.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether the rational neural subclass is dense at both extrema while preserving the exact constraint \(p_M\in C_n\) is not determined by the frozen assumptions.
obligation.obstruction: Uniform ReLU approximation of Lipschitz mechanisms and \(L^1\) histogram approximation of bounded densities control bounded-Lipschitz causal queries, but the finite code \(\kappa\) is only measurable.  Its indicator can be discontinuous on a set receiving positive probability, so those approximations need not preserve, or even approach from the feasible side of, the exact coded-law inequalities defining \(C_n\).  In addition, \(M_{\mathrm N}\) permits arbitrary finite network and histogram sizes, while \(\text{def:neural-inner-handle}\) supplies no finite architecture bound from which a global near-extremality certificate relative to the union can be derived.  Neither missing property follows from the listed support, density, Lipschitz, or rational-grammar assumptions.
obligation.attempted: The direct route couples a certifiable SCM to rational ReLU and histogram approximants and proves convergence of \(Q\); it stops at exact feasibility because convergence against a merely measurable coding indicator is unavailable.  The alternative route mixes an approximant toward an interior feasible coded law, but the frozen class is not assumed convex under such mixtures and no interior or margin condition for \(C_n\) is imposed.  Finally, fixed-architecture branch-and-bound certifies near-extremality only within that architecture, not relative to the unrestricted union defining \(M_{\mathrm N}\).
obligation.partial_result: The strongest closed reduction is the following.  If, in addition to the frozen assumptions, every \(M\in\mathcal F_{n,\mathrm{cert}}\) and every \(\delta>0\) admit \(M'\in\mathcal F_{n,\mathrm N}\) with \(|Q(M')-Q(M)|\leq\delta\), then taking approximating sequences for the lower and upper certifiable extrema gives \(\ell_{n,\mathrm N}=\ell_{n,\mathrm{cert}}\) and \(u_{n,\mathrm N}=u_{n,\mathrm{cert}}\), hence \(\Gamma_n=0\).  For any fixed finite neural architecture whose feasible parameter set has the rational compact encoding of \(\text{def:certifiable-response-program}\), the argument of \(\text{thm:rational-certificate-termination}\) also yields independently checkable \(\eta_{\mathrm{in}}\)-near-extremality certificates within that fixed architecture.  What remains open is exact-coded-law density together with a finite certificate uniformly over architecture size.
